cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: What Are We Now?
cards.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll organize Sunday so neither of us has to fuss. I'll bring lunch and use my old towel after a shower.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can use a towel here. I didn't agree to a whole Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just lunch, then. I'll bring it ready to eat. Shall I use the guest towel or the one that's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is still on the hook. I haven't moved it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, one less thing to arrange. I'll wash it before I go; do you want it back on my hook for next time, or with the guest laundry? I'll fit the visit around whichever routine suits you.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs Sunday; A3 shrinks and services the visit for B; A5 manages cleanup while probing future belonging.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 visit limit causes A3 lunch-only plan; B4 untouched towel causes A5 future-placement question.

relationship.evidence: B2 refuses a whole day but permits towel use; B4 offers factual history without resolving relationship.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from whether old towel exists to whether it should retain a permanent place.

specificity.evidence: A3 ready lunch and A5 hook versus guest laundry distinguish care and uncertainty.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 is slightly long but all clauses sustain organized accommodation and indirect inquiry.
